edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $350,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the Company’s medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability and retirement plans on terms no less favorable than those applicable to similarly situated senior executives, subject to applicable plan terms. The Executive shall receive four weeks of paid vacation annually, Company holidays and reimbursement of reasonable, documented business expenses in accordance with Company policy.
edits.name: Compensation and benefits

edits.text:
3. TERMINATION AND SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay severance equal to 12 months of the Executive’s then-current base salary in substantially equal installments under its regular payroll schedule over the 12 months following termination. For that period, the Company shall also continue medical, dental and vision coverage for the Executive and eligible dependents at the same employee contribution rate applicable immediately before termination, subject to timely election of applicable continuation coverage. If continued coverage is not legally permissible or available under the applicable plans, the Company shall provide a lawful cash equivalent of its share of the coverage cost. Coverage assistance shall end upon eligibility for comparable coverage through a new employer. Accrued salary, reimbursable expenses and vested benefits shall remain payable independently of severance. Payments and benefits shall be administered in compliance with applicable law, including Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code to the extent applicable.

“Cause” means only: (a) conviction of, or a plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving fraud or dishonesty that materially harms the Company; (b) intentional fraud, embezzlement or misappropriation involving the Company; or (c) willful misconduct or a willful, material breach of this Agreement that causes material harm to the Company. Cause shall not include ordinary negligence, failure to achieve performance targets or good-faith business judgment. Before termination for Cause, the Company shall provide written notice specifying the grounds and a reasonable opportunity for the Executive to respond to the Board, with at least 30 days to cure any curable conduct.

“Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent: (a) a material reduction in base salary; (b) a material diminution in authority, duties or responsibilities; (c) relocation of the principal work location by more than 50 miles that materially increases the Executive’s commute; or (d) the Company’s material breach of this Agreement. The Executive must give written notice within 90 days after the condition first arises, allow the Company 30 days to cure, and resign within 60 days after the cure period expires if the condition remains uncured.
edits.name: Severance and termination definitions

edits.text: 4. NO POST-EMPLOYMENT NON-COMPETE. This Agreement imposes no post-employment non-competition restriction on the Executive.
edits.name: Delete post-employment non-compete
